title: What Makes a VLA Reactive? A Study of Execution Strategies for Dynamic Manipulation
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models predict chunks of future actions, and when objects move, those chunks go stale before they are executed. We study what makes a pretrained VLA reactive, using \pihalf{} on two dynamic simulation benchmarks and three real-robot tasks. title: Bind-WAM: Binding-Uncertainty-Guided Selective Future Imagination in World Action Models
summary: World Action Models (WAMs) can improve robot learning by jointly predicting future visual states and actions, but generating a visual future at every replanning step is expensive and sometimes unnecessary. title: Scaling VLA Serving Under Robotic Execution Constraints
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising paradigm for general-purpose robotic manipulation. In our production setting, hundreds of VLA-powered robots are already operating in real-world environments, creating an immediate need for efficient fleet serving. title: Streaming Failure Forecasting: VLA Failure Monitors That Keep Learning After Deployment
summary: Failure monitors for vision-language-action (VLA) policies are trained offline and then frozen. summary: Operators can state safety constraints for robots as prohibitions such as "do not put the bowl on the stove". summary: The Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) enables scalable demonstration collection independently of a specific robot.
